To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the visual illusion of the target size affected the learning of the golf putting task.

the size of the visual illusion affected both the performance and self-efficacy of nongolf players during a practice phase, and that the effects of the visual illusion were still evident 1 day later, when the participants performed the task without the visual illusion (i.e., in the retention test).
practicing golf putting with an apparent larger hole leads to better learning outcomes, as measured by improved putting accuracy in a retention test.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how visual illusions can be used to facilitate motor skill learning.
how visual illusions can be used to enhance learning of a sport skill.
the role of visual illusions in sport skill learning and the potential of illusions as a new tool for improving motor performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
visual illusions can facilitate skill learning.
the perceived size of a target is important in the process of motor learning.
visual illusions can be a useful tool for facilitating motor skill learning, and this effect can last for at least 1 day.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perceived size of a target is important for the learning of a sport skill.
visual illusions can facilitate motor learning, even if the illusions are no longer present when the skill is being executed.
visual illusions can not only facilitate performance in the short-term, but also facilitate motor learning in the long-term.
The main takeaway from our work is that
visual illusions can be used to facilitate learning of motor skills.
the visual illusion technique can facilitate learning in the absence of the illusion.
the visual illusion of target size may facilitate motor skill learning.
